args.budget_revisions: Overrun prevalence is associated with the number of budget revisions to date. Snapshots with zero revisions show an overrun prevalence of 51.7% (95% interval: 49.0% to 54.4%), with a mean gap of 1,965.3 ILS. Snapshots with one revision show a prevalence of 25.0% (95% interval: 18.9% to 32.3%), with a mean gap of -19,637.9 ILS. Snapshots with two or more revisions show a prevalence of 9.8% (95% interval: 4.6% to 19.8%), with a mean gap of -39,325.5 ILS. The association suggests that snapshots with more revisions tend to have lower overrun prevalence and more negative gaps.
args.correlations: On the train group (1,084 snapshots), the strongest Spearman correlation with the signed gap is over_plan_pre_vat at 0.266, indicating a weak positive association. Budget_revisions_to_date shows a Spearman correlation of -0.246, a weak negative association. The point-biserial correlation with is_overrun shows over_plan_pre_vat at 0.275 and budget_revisions_to_date at -0.183. Other features show correlations with absolute values below 0.13, indicating weak associations. No feature shows a strong correlation with the signed gap or overrun status.
args.data_quality: Of 1,600 scheduled snapshots, 1,538 remained eligible after Policy C applied deterministically. Sixty-two snapshots became ineligible: 50 due to commitment_category_missing and 12 due to manual_cost_undated. Ineligibility was distributed across stages as S0: 3 snapshots, S1: 14 snapshots, S2: 20 snapshots, and S3: 25 snapshots. Among 400 productions, 375 were fully eligible, 3 were fully ineligible, and 22 had at least one ineligible snapshot. No productions were flagged as target_unreliable. The cleaning process identified 42 records with problems and dropped 107 exact duplicates across three tables; normalisations were applied deterministically without imputation.
args.fee_terms: Overrun prevalence by fee mode shows that snapshots with an amount-based fee have a prevalence of 52.6% (95% interval: 48.4% to 56.8%), while those with a percent-based fee have a prevalence of 44.5% (95% interval: 41.4% to 47.6%). By fee inclusion, snapshots where the fee is included in the budget show an overrun prevalence of 48.7% (95% interval: 45.3% to 52.1%), while those where the fee is not included show a prevalence of 45.8% (95% interval: 42.2% to 49.4%). The mean gap for snapshots with the fee included is -466.4 ILS, compared to -3,430.3 ILS when the fee is not included.
args.frozen_split: The frozen split test minus train difference in overrun prevalence is 14.7 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval: 3.3 pp to 26.2 pp), with the interval not including zero. The test group has 306 snapshots from 80 productions with an overrun prevalence of 59.2% (95% bootstrap interval: 48.4% to 69.5%), the train group has 1,084 snapshots from 278 productions with a prevalence of 44.5% (95% interval: 38.9% to 50.2%), and the demo group has 148 snapshots from 39 productions with a prevalence of 43.9% (95% interval: 29.7% to 59.2%). The split is frozen, not tuned; this difference is a sampling outcome documented when the split was frozen.
args.limitations: The analysis is descriptive and does not establish causation or predict outcomes. Correlations are computed on the train group only and are weak across all features, limiting their explanatory power. The frozen split difference, while statistically distinct from zero, reflects the sampling outcome at the time the split was frozen and should not be interpreted as evidence of systematic differences between groups. The signed gap and overrun definitions are based on the P2 contract and do not include payments or commitment totals. The analysis does not assess the real-world accuracy of the synthetic data or recommend re-splitting or rebalancing the frozen split.
args.overview: The exploratory data analysis examines 1,538 eligible snapshots from 397 productions across four event stages (S0, S1, S2, S3) and three frozen split groups (train, test, demo). The data includes four event archetypes: bar/bat mitzvah, conference, corporate, and wedding. The signed gap is the verified final cost plus the contractual fee when included in the budget, minus the approved budget in effect at the snapshot (ILS, pre-VAT); a positive gap indicates over budget and a negative gap indicates under budget. The analysis measures overrun prevalence (the signed gap exceeds 0.5 ILS) and material overrun prevalence (the signed gap exceeds 2% of the budget).

## Observations (descriptive, from eligible synthetic snapshots)

The 1,538 eligible snapshots come from 397 productions: 375 fully eligible and 22 partially eligible (3 of the 400 scheduled productions have no eligible snapshot).

Overall overrun prevalence is 47.3% (95% Wilson interval: 44.8% to 49.8%), with 728 overrun snapshots among 1,538 eligible snapshots. Material overrun prevalence is 35.7% (95% interval: 33.3% to 38.1%), with 549 snapshots.

Overrun prevalence varies by stage. S0 shows 51.6% (95% interval: 46.7% to 56.5%), S1 shows 49.7% (95% interval: 44.8% to 54.7%), S2 shows 44.7% (95% interval: 39.8% to 49.8%), and S3 shows 42.9% (95% interval: 38.0% to 48.0%). The prevalence decreases from early to final stages.

The signed gap distribution has a median of -988.9 ILS and a mean of -1,863.6 ILS, with a standard deviation of 29,821.0 ILS. The 5th to 95th percentile range is -46,958.0 ILS to 41,310.1 ILS.

Overrun prevalence by frozen split group shows train at 44.5% (95% bootstrap interval: 38.9% to 50.2%) from 1,084 snapshots, test at 59.2% (95% bootstrap interval: 48.4% to 69.5%) from 306 snapshots, and demo at 43.9% (95% bootstrap interval: 29.7% to 59.2%) from 148 snapshots.

## Hypotheses for Crew 2 (not predictions)

Does the stage progression reflect genuine budget control improvements, or does it reflect selection effects in which productions advance to later stages?

Are the differences in overrun prevalence between fee modes (fixed, percentage, variable) associated with different cost structures or risk profiles?

Does the number of budget revisions to date correlate with overrun risk, and if so, is this association driven by reactive revision patterns or by underlying project complexity?

How do commitment category diversity and the temporal spread of costs (recency and age measures) relate to overrun occurrence?

## Frozen split note

The frozen split was not tuned and was assigned deterministically as a sampling outcome independent of the outcome mechanism. The test group shows higher overrun prevalence than the train group. The test minus train difference in overrun prevalence is 14.7 percentage points (95% bootstrap interval: 3.3 pp to 26.2 pp), assessed as a production-level bootstrap in frozen_split_prevalence_difference in stats.json.

## Data quality and Policy C exclusions

Of 1,600 scheduled snapshots, 62 became ineligible under Policy C: 50 due to commitment_category_missing and 12 due to manual_cost_undated. By stage, ineligibility was distributed as S0: 3 snapshots, S1: 14 snapshots, S2: 20 snapshots, and S3: 25 snapshots.

The cleaning process identified 42 records with problems across three tables: 24 records in commitments with missing category values, 3 records in manual_costs lacking created_date values, and 15 records in payments with out-of-range amount_gross values. Exact duplicates were dropped: 22 from commitments, 16 from manual_costs, and 69 from payments. Normalisations were applied deterministically without imputation across all tables.

Among 400 productions, 375 were fully eligible, 3 were fully ineligible, and 25 had at least one ineligible snapshot. No productions were flagged as target_unreliable.

## Limitations

These data are synthetic and have not been validated against real-world budget outcomes. The observations and associations described here are properties of the synthetic dataset and do not constitute evidence of real-world accuracy or predictive validity. The handoff is complete and the split is frozen; no re-splitting or rebalancing is recommended.
